abstract.para: The command btrfs subvolume creates, lists, shows and deletes subvolumes and snapshots. The following procedures use a Btrfs file system that is mounted at /mnt.

section.title: Creating a subvolume
section.para: Create a subvolume to keep a directory tree separate from other data.

section.title: Creating a snapshot of a subvolume
section.para: To capture the current state of a subvolume, create a snapshot of it. Add the option -r to create a read-only snapshot.

section.title: Listing subvolumes and snapshots
section.para: Subvolumes and snapshots are listed together. To see all of them, run the following command:
section.screen: &prompt.sudo;btrfs subvolume list /mnt ID 256 gen 12 top level 5 path projects ID 257 gen 14 top level 5 path projects-snapshot
section.para: The value top level 5 shows that the parent is the top-level subvolume. To list only snapshots, add the option -s.

section.title: Deleting a subvolume or snapshot
section.para: Deleting a subvolume removes its data and all nested subvolumes.

warning.title: Deleting a subvolume removes its data
warning.para: Deleting a subvolume destroys all files in it and in its nested subvolumes. You cannot undo this action.
Before you delete a subvolume, make sure that a backup exists or that you no longer need the data.

step.para: Verify that the snapshot no longer appears in the output of sudo btrfs subvolume list /mnt.

section.para: Btrfs frees the space of a deleted subvolume in the background. The free space can increase for some time after the command finishes.
